summary: apt module options for policy-rc.d exit codes, purging config files, package state (present, latest, absent, build-dep, fixed), updating the cache with retries, and system upgrade modes.
questions: How do I prevent services from starting after package install using apt?
How do I remove a package and its config files?
How do I make sure a package is the newest version?
How do I fix broken dependencies with Ansible apt?
How do I run a dist-upgrade with Ansible?
How do I retry apt-get update if it fails?

answer_card.title: apt options: state, purge, upgrade
answer_card.answer_md:
- `state` (default `present`): `absent`, `build-dep`, `latest`, `present`, `fixed` (repair broken deps)
- `purge`: remove config files with `state=absent` or `autoremove`
- `policy_rc_d`: e.g. `101` stops services auto-starting; existing file is backed up and restored
- `update_cache`: run `apt-get update` first (default off); `update_cache_retries` (5), `update_cache_retry_max_delay` (12s backoff)
- `upgrade`: `no` (default), `yes`/`safe`, `full`, `dist`. Upgrades the system, not one package (use `state=latest` for that)
